turns.question: Using the Q3 2026 service level report and the MSA, what service credit is Voss-Lindqvist owed for August 2026?
turns.text:
The service credit that Voss-Lindqvist AB is owed for August 2026 is calculated based on the terms of the Master Services Agreement (DEMO) and the Q3 2026 service level report.

According to the Master Services Agreement (DEMO), if Availability in a calendar month is below the Availability Target, Provider shall give Client a Service Credit equal to the following percentage of the Monthly Subscription Fee for that month [11].

The Q3 2026 service level report indicates that the Availability in August 2026 was 98.71%, which falls within the range of 98.0% or more but below 99.0%, entitling the Client to a 10% Service Credit [5].

The Monthly Subscription Fee is stated as USD 18,500 [9].

The Service Credit for August 2026 is therefore calculated as 10% of USD 18,500, which equals USD 1,850 [11].

The Master Services Agreement (DEMO) also states that the total Service Credits for any calendar month shall not exceed thirty percent (30%) of the Monthly Subscription Fee for that month [11].

Since USD 1,850 is less than 30% of USD 18,500, the Service Credit of USD 1,850 is within the cap [11].

Therefore, the service credit that Voss-Lindqvist AB is owed for August 2026 is USD 1,850.

turns.question: If the service credit clause is applied correctly to the April, May and June 2026 figures, what should the service credits total?

For June 2026, the shortfall is 3 full percentage points below the KPI, as stated in source 2. The service credit for June 2026 is calculated as 3 × 5% × GBP 140,000 = GBP 21,000 [2].

The total service credits for April, May, and June 2026 are GBP 42,000 + GBP 35,000 + GBP 21,000 = GBP 98,000 [2].

The maximum cap for service credits is 25% of the monthly fee, which is GBP 35,000 per month, as stated in source 6. The total service credits for the three months, GBP 98,000, do not exceed the annual liability cap of GBP 400,000, as stated in source 1. [1].

Therefore, the service credits for April, May, and June 2026, when calculated correctly under the service credit clause, total GBP 98,000.

turns.question: And which parts of it are binding?
turns.text:
The documents indicate that certain parts of the term sheet are binding. Specifically, Sections 1 through 10 of the term sheet are binding upon execution, as stated in the document: "This Term Sheet is non-binding except for the provisions set forth in Sections 1 through 10, which shall be binding upon the parties upon execution" [1].

Other terms and conditions in the term sheet are subject to negotiation and execution of definitive agreements. The binding sections include the entire agreement clause, which states: "This Term Sheet constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements, understandings, and negotiations, whether written or oral" [1].

The non-binding nature of other sections is also confirmed, as the document states: "All other terms and conditions shall be subject to negotiation and execution of definitive agreements" [1].

The term sheet also includes other binding provisions, such as the governing law clause: "This Term Sheet shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles" [2].

The closing date is also a binding provision, as the document states: "The closing of the Investment (the 'Closing') shall occur on 30 October 2026, subject to the satisfaction of all conditions set forth in this Term Sheet and the definitive agreements to be entered into by the parties" [2].

The Board has also approved the closing date of 30 October 2026 for the Series A Financing, as stated in the document: "The Board hereby approves the proposed closing date of 30 October 2026 for the Series A Financing" [3].

The term sheet also includes a binding provision regarding the option pool top-up: "The Company shall top up the option pool to a total of 12% of the post-money capitalization of the Company immediately following the closing of the Investment" [2].

However, the draft Stock Purchase Agreement is inconsistent with the term sheet regarding the option pool top-up, as stated in the document: "the draft Stock Purchase Agreement dated 20 September 2026, which contains an inconsistency regarding the option pool top-up, shall be revised to reflect the terms set forth in the Term Sheet" [3].

The term sheet also includes a binding provision regarding the liquidation preference: "the Term Sheet provides for a 1x non-participating liquidation preference" [4].

The term sheet also includes a binding provision regarding the board composition: "The Company’s board of directors will consist of five members: two founders, one designee of Aldermoor Ventures LP, and two independent directors" [6].

The term sheet also includes a binding provision regarding protective provisions: "Protective provisions will be in place for the Series A investors, requiring their approval for certain material decisions" [6].
